text: | name | text | yes | format(two names separated by one space) |

comments.text: The format rule admits exactly two space-separated tokens, which rejects real names like "Mary Jane Watson", "Jean-Luc Picard" or "Ludwig van Beethoven" (multi-part and hyphenated). Consider whether the rule should be "two or more tokens separated by spaces" or whether one free-text field is the wrong model at all (see the comment on age). Also: no max length is set — a max(100) or similar would bound the column.

Two modelling concerns. (1) A stored age goes stale the moment the person has a birthday — a date of birth (date kind) is the usual register field and age becomes derived; storing age is only right if the value is an intake snapshot. (2) max(70) silently excludes people over 70 — confirm that is a genuine business rule of this register and not an arbitrary cap; if it is real, say so in the notes so a reader does not mistake it for a placeholder.

text: | gndr | choice(male, female, other) | no | the person's gender; renamed from `gender` at the author's request; [ASSUMED: values male/female/other, optional — say the word to change] |

comments.text: The [ASSUMED] marker is still live: the values (male/female/other) and the field being optional are unconfirmed defaults, and a surviving marker blocks the freeze. Confirm or change them so the marker can come off. Separately: `gndr` as a field id becomes the entity property, the form control id and the API name — an unusual abbreviation for a three-value field. If it was chosen for brevity, `gender` costs three characters and reads cleaner everywhere downstream.
sad

No uniqueness is declared on any field, so duplicate rows (same name, age and gender) are allowed and the search screen will list them side by side. If this register is meant to hold one row per person, name — or the pair name+age — needs a uniqueness rule in the notes; if duplicates are fine, no change is needed, but that is worth stating as a decision rather than leaving as an omission.
